title: format_table shows wrong column widths
description: format_table renders a list of rows as a padded text table. The output has wrong column widths — columns are too narrow and data is truncated. The error shows up in format_table's output, but the formatting logic itself is correct; investigate what it depends on.

hidden_tests.test_table.py:
from table import column_widths, format_table


def test_column_widths():
    rows = [["name", "age"], ["Alice", "30"], ["Bob", "7"]]
    assert column_widths(rows) == [5, 3]


def test_column_widths_empty():
    assert column_widths([]) == []


def test_format_table():
    rows = [["name", "age"], ["Alice", "30"], ["Bob", "7"]]
    result = format_table(rows)
    lines = result.split("\n")
    assert len(lines) == 3
    assert "Alice" in lines[1]
    assert lines[0].startswith("name ")
    # Columns must be padded to the max width.
    assert lines[2].startswith("Bob  ")


def test_format_single_column():
    rows = [["hello"], ["hi"]]
    result = format_table(rows)
    assert result == "hello\nhi   "
